summary.short: Taiwan's Artificial Intelligence Basic Act, promulgated 14 January ROC year 115 and in force from promulgation, sets principles for AI research, development and application and directs central and local governments to promote AI, support industry and manage high-risk uses under risk-based rules.
summary.long: The Act sets seven principles for AI research, development and application (Art. 4): sustainability and welfare, human autonomy, privacy and data governance, security, transparency and explainability, fairness and non-discrimination, and accountability. It requires the government to avoid harmful or discriminatory AI uses (Art. 5) and to designate high-risk AI applications, which must carry warnings (Art. 5(2)). It creates a National AI Strategy Special Committee under the Executive Yuan (Art. 6), and directs the government to promote education, budgets, subsidies, tax and financial incentives, with an annual performance reporting system (Arts. 7–10). It allows innovation experimental environments (Art. 11), calls for data sharing and reuse and minimisation of personal data by sectoral agencies (Arts. 13–14), and sets labour-related duties (Art. 15). The Ministry of Digital Development is to build a risk classification framework and sectoral agencies are to issue risk-based management rules (Art. 16). The government is to define liability and relief mechanisms for high-risk applications (Art. 17), review existing laws within two years (Art. 18), and assess risks of its own AI use (Art. 19). The text contains no private-sector penalty provisions.

notes: No other instrument is named in the text. References to 其他法律 (Art. 1) and to 法規 (Art. 18) are generic, and references to 本法 (e.g., Arts. 11, 16) and to Art. 5 para. 1 are internal, so the relations list is empty. The only date in the text is the promulgation date in the header (民國 115 年 01 月 14 日); Art. 20 makes the act effective on the promulgation date, and no external event is recorded. Art. 17 para. 2 excludes pre-application AI research and development from para. 1 liability rules, except real-environment testing or provision of products or services. Competence is split: Art. 2 gives the central competent authority to the National Science and Technology Council, while Art. 16 assigns the risk classification framework to the Ministry of Digital Affairs and Art. 5 para. 2 requires high-risk designation by the central industry authority in consultation with the Ministry of Digital Affairs. The text does not state a conflict.

relations.note: The text names no other statute, regulation or instrument; its cross-references are generic (其他法律, 法規) or internal to this act (本法 and its article numbers).

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in the operative provisions changes legal treatment. The two-year period in Art. 18 is a procedural time limit (an event, not a threshold). Art. 5(2) designates high-risk applications by government determination with no numeric criterion. Art. 16 refers to risk classes without numbers, and Art. 10 and Art. 17 contain no numeric cutoffs.
